preventive_first.title: Protect a 30-minute wind-down
preventive_first.body: Start a fixed wind-down 30 minutes before your target bedtime: dim lights, screens off, and 5 minutes of slow breathing or stretching. Keep the same start time for 7 nights.

physiological_first.title: Lock a 7–8 hour sleep window
physiological_first.body: Choose a sleep window of 7–8 hours (for example 23:00–07:00) and protect it for the next 7 nights before raising training load or adding new goals.

behavioral_first.title: Attach a 10-minute starter habit
behavioral_first.body: Pick one daily cue (after morning coffee or right after lunch) and run a 10-minute starter — brisk walk, mobility, or journaling — every day this week.

lifestyle.title: Morning light + 20-minute walk
lifestyle.body: Get 10–15 minutes of outdoor daylight within an hour of waking, and add one brisk 20-minute walk on at least 5 days this week.

risk_awareness.title: Log two early signals nightly
risk_awareness.body: Each evening, note sleep hours and peak stress (1–10). If either worsens for 3 days in a row, schedule a clinician check-in; use Health Guide only for educational framing.

performance.title: Match effort with equal recovery
performance.body: After every hard training or deep-work block, schedule an equal recovery block (easy walk, quiet time, or earlier lights-out). Cap hard days at 4 this week.

lifestyle.title: Screens-off by a fixed clock time
lifestyle.body: Set a phone/laptop cutoff 45 minutes before bed (same clock time nightly). Replace that slot with reading or light stretching for 7 days.

risk_awareness.title: Three-day early-warning rule
risk_awareness.body: If sleep drops below your usual by 60+ minutes or stress stays ≥7/10 for 3 consecutive days, book a clinician consult and pause new experiments.

performance.title: Deload before you push
performance.body: Keep intensity at maintenance for 5 days: no personal records, and end each session with 10 minutes of easy movement or breathwork.

lifestyle.title: Same wake time ±15 minutes
lifestyle.body: Wake within a 15-minute window every day this week (including one weekend day). Pair it with water and daylight before caffeine.

risk_awareness.title: Rest-day checkpoint
risk_awareness.body: Schedule two lighter days. On those days, record resting mood and any new symptoms for 2 minutes — escalate to a clinician if something new persists.

performance.title: Recovery floor before load
performance.body: Require at least 7 hours in bed and one 15-minute easy walk on the day before any hard session. Skip the hard session if either is missed.

lifestyle.title: Habit stack: meal → 2-minute reset
lifestyle.body: After lunch, take 2 minutes of nasal breathing or a hallway walk before sitting again. Repeat after dinner for 7 days.

risk_awareness.title: Cue a 60-second body scan
risk_awareness.body: At a fixed evening alarm, do a 60-second check: pain, breath, mood. Write one line. Bring the log to a clinician if a new pattern appears.

performance.title: Calendar the work–recover pair
performance.body: Block focus/training and the matching recovery slot on your calendar for the next 5 workdays so recovery is not optional.

questionnaire.title: Fill the remaining questionnaire gaps
questionnaire.body: Your questionnaire is {{percent}}% complete. Spend 10–15 minutes on the thinnest sections so the next report can name sharper, more personal actions.

service.title: Return to {{service}} after one trial
service.body: Practice one recommendation for 7 days, then reopen {{service}} and note what felt easier in one short sentence.

devices.title: Optional: link one wearable
devices.body: When ready, connect a wearable so sleep and movement trends can sit beside your questionnaire — still as trends, not diagnoses.

devicesActive.title: Review 7 days of device trends
devicesActive.body: Open the last week from your {{count}} linked device(s). Circle one pattern (sleep, steps, or resting pulse) that matches how you felt, and keep that metric for the habit you chose.
